proposed.text: A 1000 mm escalator operates at Salvan's rated-speed limit of 38 m/min (the maximum allowed along the incline) and is projected to carry 5,500 passengers/hour during peak periods. If demand increases and a second identical escalator is installed, what is the total system capacity, and what factors could limit this theoretical maximum?

options.text: 11,000 persons/hour with no limiting factors, assuming perfect conditions
11,000 persons/hour maximum theoretical; actual throughput limited by landing congestion, dwell time, and step spacing geometry
7,500 persons/hour; the second escalator reduces individual capacity by interference effects
6,750 persons/hour per unit; two units operate at reduced speed to prevent overloading

proposed.rationale: Two identical escalators can theoretically deliver 11,000 persons/hour (2 x 5,500). Actual throughput is limited by landing congestion, passenger dwell time on steps, step spacing geometry, and balancing passenger loads between units. The speed basis is aligned to Salvan's rated-speed limit of 38 m/min used in the article body. Source: Salvan Architectural Utilities 2 (escalator rated speed max 38 m/min along the incline).
proposed.explanation: Two 5,500 persons/hour escalators deliver 11,000 persons/hour theoretical maximum, limited in practice by landing congestion and dwell time. Speed basis = 38 m/min per the article body.
